text: Casey Lindqvist wants node pools and autoscaling ceilings pinned with real headroom, so capacity doesn't depend on an autoscaler reacting fast enough during the next sale. Dana Whitfield pushes back immediately: pinning everything high rebuilds the exact over-provisioning problem FinOps exists to prevent.

Casey's position is fair: a repeat incident costs more in trust and on-call burden than most plausible wasted spend, and a simple, legible policy doesn't depend on anyone reading a utilization chart correctly next quarter.

Dana's position is equally fair: the incident wasn't caused by too little total capacity, it was caused by an uneven distribution of the capacity that already existed. More capacity, spread the same unsafe way, doesn't obviously fix that.

Splitting the difference between two unmeasured guesses doesn't produce a right answer. What's actually missing from this conversation is the real, measured per-AZ peak-load data the sale already produced — and nobody has brought it into the room yet.
